record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Given a graph G, can it be decided in polynomial time whether G has a Type-A order or a Type-B order of its vertices? For a linear order v1,...,vn, d−(vi) is the number of neighbors of vi appearing earlier and d+(vi) is the number appearing later; a Type-A order requires every d−(v) to be odd or 0, while a Type-B order allows either that Type-A condition or the alternative that d−(v) is even and d+(v)=0.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a graph G admits a Type-A order, or a Type-B order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple graph with vertex set V = {v_1,...,v_n}. For a linear ordering v_1,...,v_n of V, and for each vertex v_i, define
  d^-(v_i) = |{ j < i : v_j v_i ∈ E }|,  d^+(v_i) = |{ j > i : v_j v_i ∈ E }|.
Call the ordering a Type-A order if for every vertex v, d^-(v) is either 0 or odd.
Call the ordering a Type-B order if for every vertex v, either d^-(v) is 0 or odd, or else d^-(v) is even and d^+(v) = 0.

Question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G, decides whether G admits a Type-A order? Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether G admits a Type-B order?
